$comment: Civil penalties for late filing/payment + EOPT taxpayer classification.

legalBasis: RA 11976 (EOPT); reduced 10% surcharge for micro & small taxpayers
surcharge.notes: The reduced 10% applies to micro & small taxpayers for returns due on or after Jan 22, 2024, when EOPT took effect (it is not retroactive); returns due earlier keep 25%. EOPT also removed the 25% surcharge for filing at the wrong venue. The 50% surcharge covers willful neglect to file AND willfully false/fraudulent returns (underdeclaring sales by more than 30% or overstating deductions by more than 30% is prima facie fraud) and is NOT reduced for micro/small taxpayers (only the 25% drops to 10%). The 25% also applies to unpaid deficiency assessments and partial payments, not just late returns.

legalBasis: NIRC Sec 249, as amended by RA 10963 (double the BSP legal rate of 6%)
NIRC Sec 249 before RA 10963 (20% a year, for days before Jan 1, 2018)
NIRC Sec 249(A), as amended by RA 10963 (proviso: no simultaneous deficiency and delinquency interest)
RA 11976 (EOPT); 50% of the rate for micro & small taxpayers
interest.notes: 12% per annum confirmed current as of October 7, 2026 (in force since TRAIN, Jan 1, 2018); days before Jan 1, 2018 are charged at the old 20%, so a period that spans that date is split. Micro & small taxpayers pay 6% on returns due on or after Jan 22, 2024 (EOPT is not retroactive). Deficiency and delinquency interest never run simultaneously.

legalBasis: NIRC Sec 249(A) (interest runs from the date prescribed for payment until full payment)
RMC 65-2016 (a deadline on a weekend or holiday moves to the next working day)
interestDayCount.notes: Interest counts each day from the day after the due date through the payment date. When the due date falls on a weekend or holiday it first moves to the next working day, and interest counts from the day after that working day (RMC 65-2016). Days are divided by 365, also in leap years: this is a default not yet confirmed against the RR 21-2018 illustrations or eBIRForms (on a 366-day basis, a year late across Feb 29 gives ₱12,000.00 instead of ₱12,032.88 per ₱100,000 at 12%). When the rate changes during the period (20% to 12% on Jan 1, 2018), each part is computed and rounded to the centavo separately and the parts are added.

eoptTransition.notes: Micro & small taxpayers get the 10% surcharge and 6% interest only for returns due on or after Jan 22, 2024 (the due date after moving off a weekend or holiday). Default not yet confirmed: tax that fell due before Jan 22, 2024 and is still unpaid after it keeps the rates in force on its due date (25% surcharge, 12% interest) for the whole period, with no switch to 6%. Also unconfirmed: whether returns due between Jan 22 and Apr 26, 2024 (before RR 6-2024 took effect) get the reduced rates; the calculator gives them.

legalBasis: RMO 7-2015 Annex A (failure to file/pay, NIRC Sec 255), confirmed still the operative schedule as of Aug 2026, superseding RMO 19-2007
RR 6-2024: the 50% compromise reduction for micro & small taxpayers covers only invoicing violations (NIRC Secs 113, 237 and 238) not involving fraud, so it does not apply to late filing or payment
compromiseTiers.notes: Compromise penalties are settlements in lieu of criminal prosecution and are consensual/negotiable; the schedule is the BIR's standard ask. The schedule follows RMO 7-2015 Annex A and is the same for every taxpayer size: late filing or payment is a Sec 255 violation, which the EOPT 50% reduction does not cover. A tax due of ₱0 (nil return filed late) falls in the first tier (₱1,000). The schedule covers only violations that do not involve fraud: for a willfully false or fraudulent return (50% surcharge) the calculator shows the compromise as not on the standard schedule, since such a case may be referred for prosecution instead. Still worth a CPA's eye before quoting a client.

classification.notes: Classification is by gross sales (business income only); micro & small taxpayers get the reduced surcharge/interest, halved Sec 250 penalties, and 50% off the compromise penalty for invoicing violations only (Secs 113, 237 and 238, not involving fraud). The compromise for late filing or payment (Sec 255) is not reduced. The classification is independent of Top Withholding Agent designation; a 'small' taxpayer can still be a TWA.

legalBasis: RA 11976 (EOPT) & RR 6-2024 (halved amounts for micro & small taxpayers)
infoReturnPenalty.notes: ₱1,000 for EACH failure to file an information return, statement, list, or required attachment (SAWT, SLSP, QAP, alphalists, eAFS uploads), capped at ₱25,000 aggregate per calendar year (₱500 per failure / ₱12,500 cap for micro & small taxpayers). The amounts are per failure, not a flat cap. Late attachments don't make a timely-filed return late; the exposure is this penalty plus credit-disallowance and deemed-not-filed risks.
